name: Ghost White
lede: Ghost White is a computer color name from the X11 set: a white tipped faintly toward blue.

sections.title: One of 140
sections.body: Paterson counts Ghost White among the 140 colours of the X11 set and gives its hex code as #F8F8FF [1]. In his colour index it is filed among the whites with Floral White, Ivory and Antique White [2]. Beyond that, the books say nothing about where the name came from [1][2].

sections.title: Cool white and warm white
sections.body: Compare it with its sibling [[floral-white]], which leans yellow, and with [[alice-blue]], a paler blue-tinted name in the same family [3]. Plain [[white]] and [[ivory]] sit on the other side [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The hex #F8F8FF measures lightness 97.8, chroma 3.6 and hue angle 290 degrees, a blue-violet tint so slight that it reads as white on most screens [3]. The word "ghost" is a naming choice, not a measurement, and no source ties it to anything specific [1][3]. In plain numbers, the hex #F8F8FF sets red and green at 248 and blue at 255, so the tint comes from blue sitting a little higher than the other two channels [3]. That is the mirror of Floral White, where blue sits lower than the others [3].

origin.first_recorded: X11 color set (date not given in the books)
